title: Orchestrator slim handoff and opaque KV API cleanup
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Reduce tail allocations, simplify the continuous-batcher -> orchestrator handoff, and introduce a minimal opaque KV interface to decouple eviction/migration logic from callers. This ticket converts the current tight coupling between the scheduler and the KV cache into a small, well-defined API; removes the global slot-grab spin path used during high contention; and reuses lightweight slab-like frames for batch payloads to reduce GC/allocator churn.

Background: Over the past year we've accumulated several incremental patches to the batch handoff code that fixed correctness and live-lock cases but increased allocation churn and lock contention. The current path allocates transient batch frames per request, performs atomic KV lookups inline under the scheduler lock, and uses a global handoff list that degenerates under bursty ingress. We've seen high p99 latency and elevated memory churn in stress tests (batch_latency_p99 spikes, allocator-cross-heap events).

Goals:
- Define an OpaqueKV interface (get_snapshot, async_prefetch, release_snapshot, hint_eviction) to isolate eviction and priming semantics from callers.
- Replace per-request batch-frame allocation with a small pool-backed slab for short-lived frames; ensure frames are recycled deterministically on handoff/failure paths.
- Replace the global spinlock handoff queue with per-worker bounded MPSC queues and a light cooperative-steal path to avoid a single hot queue.
- Keep behavior backwards-compatible for external callers; introduce feature-flagged rollout to ensure fast rollback if regressions occur.

Design notes / tradeoffs:
- OpaqueKV is intentionally minimal: it returns an immutable snapshot handle that contains pointers into cache-backed memory or compressed backing storage. Callers must call release_snapshot; we will add diagnostic leak detection. This avoids copying KV slots for the common hot-path while preventing callers from depending on internal eviction policies.
- Pool-backed frames reduce allocations but require careful zeroing to avoid leaking secrets; pool reclaim will sanitize frames on release.
- Per-worker queues increase memory slightly but significantly reduce contention; worst-case steal adds a small scheduling cost but reduces p99 latency under bursts.

Implementation plan:
1) Add the OpaqueKV trait and a shim adapter for the existing KV store (branch: feature/opaque-kv). Create unit tests for snapshot lifecycle and leak detection.
2) Implement frame pool as a lock-free freelist with epoch reclamation; wire into batch submit path behind a runtime feature flag.
3) Replace global handoff queue with bounded per-worker MPSC queues and implement cooperative work-stealing to handle skew.
4) End-to-end test: run stress harness (ingress-bursts), record batch_latency_ms, kv_miss_ratio, eviction_ops/sec, allocator_cross_allocs.
5) Canary rollout: route 5% of traffic in dedicated-us-west region, monitor for 48h, then ramp to 25% and full roll as metrics stabilize.

Monitoring & dashboards: New dashboard panels expected:
- batch_latency.{p50,p90,p99}_ms (goal: p99 -20%),
- allocator_cross_allocs/min (goal: -30%),
- kv_snapshot_leaks (goal: 0 after tests),
- handoff_contention_retries/sec (goal: -> 0 under bursts),
- memory_tail_percentile (p99 mem usage goal: -25%).

Acceptance criteria:
- Integration tests exercising failure paths (cache eviction during use, snapshot release under timeout) pass in CI.
- Canary 48h: no increase in error rate or user-observed latency on affected routes; p99 latency improvement >= 12% on synthetic burst tests; allocator_cross_allocs drop >= 25%.
- No snapshot leaks observed in canary; leak detector counters remain zero in steady-state.
- Documentation: Confluence doc describing OpaqueKV contract and migration notes published and linked in PR.

Rollback plan: Disable feature flag and revert to the previous handoff path; pool allocations are non-destructive if disabled.

Notes for reviewers: Pay attention to the OpaqueKV lifetime model - snapshots must be explicitly released. The freelist uses epoch-based reclamation that requires per-worker quiescence points; ensure shutdown path signals quiescence before process exit.

Estimated effort: ~5 points (2 dev days + 2 code-review/e2e + canary monitoring).
